newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish external reserves 5.72 bln punts at end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Irish external reserves 5.72 bln punts at end-Sept.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves rose by 568 million punts to 5.722 billion in September, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
"Positive foreign exchange market intervention, EU receipts and Exchequer foreign borrowing during the month contributed to this development," the central bank said.
Analysts had forecast a rise in reserves to between 5.35 and 6.0 billion, as they believed the bank had been a net seller of the Irish pound in September to slow its advance against the German mark.
"Positive Irish-pound funding added to net tax receipts and EU transfers contributed to an increase of 495 million in government balances at the central bank," the central bank said in a statement.
Irish pound credit to the government by domestic credit institutions fell by 422 million punts during the month due to a fall in their holdings of government bonds, it said.
"Redemptions totalling 483 million punts on 30 September were almost all bonds held by residents," the central bank said.

"Non-resident holdings of Irish government securities increased by 461 million during the month, reflecting generally strong demand for the higher-yielding EU government bonds on foot of convergence expectations."

The central bank said money-market support through the Short Term Facility (STF) rate and security repurchase agreements, less overnight and fixed term deposits at the central bank, was 531 million punts.
This represented a fall of 67 million punts compared with end-August, it said.

"Net tax receipts, positive Irish-pound funding and the effects of NTMA transactions with commercial banks were exceeded by substantial positive foreign-exchange market interventions," the central bank said.
